canDo: Can complete a timed mini B2 mock exam: listening 30 minutes, reading 60 minutes, writing 60 minutes, speaking 30 minutes’ preparation + 20 minutes’ performance, staying within time on each part while keeping your language accurate.
review: Review day 2’s subjunctive (vouloir que, regretter que, douter que, il faut que, craindre que… ne) and day 6’s expressions of result (si bien que, de sorte que, au point que, tellement… que, d’où), drawing on the listening/reading strategies and writing/speaking frameworks from days 29–38.
input: Read (60 minutes): a long article on sleep deprivation, an editorial against secondary school league tables and a forum post about a “tool library” in Lausanne, Switzerland; listen (30 minutes): an interview on how volunteering is changing (twice), an interview on the urban heat island effect (twice) and a local news flash on a municipal bike repair grant (once). Follow the real exam order: listening first, then reading.
output: Write (60 minutes): a forum post giving your view on “should employees be allowed to bring their dogs to work?” (≥250 words); speak (30 minutes’ preparation): a 6-minute monologue on a document about “street advertising”, then a 5-minute debate with the examiner on “a law banning screens for children under three”.
checkpoint: Combined listening + reading accuracy ≥75% (i.e. ≥37 out of 50); essay finished within 60 minutes, ≥250 words, with 5 minutes left for checking; monologue at least 5 minutes; no part overruns. Record the time spent and the points lost on each part for the day 40 review.
challenge: Today’s challenge: pick any society news item on RFI’s « Journal en français facile » and give yourself 10 minutes: listen once, write down 3 key points, then write one comment of your own with « si bien que » and one with « il faut que »; keep it with today’s mock-exam timesheet.

questions.why: The article gives sleep-deprivation data first (paragraph 1), then consequences (paragraph 2), causes (paragraph 3), remedies (paragraph 4) and obstacles (paragraph 5). Neither A nor C is covered.
« À court terme, la concentration baisse… si bien que les erreurs se multiplient ». B is a “long-term” risk; C is the opposite of « l’humeur se dégrade ».
« refuse qu’on en fasse le seul bouc émissaire : « Il faut que l’on regarde aussi l’organisation du travail » ». A is exactly what she objects to; B: she doesn’t deny that screens have an effect.

The day is taken up by work and commuting, so the evening is the only time “that belongs to them”, which is why they don’t want to go to bed early. A is the opposite of the context; C reads appartenir too literally.
« autorisent de courtes siestes… au point que des salles de repos font leur apparition dans les bureaux ». B and C aren’t mentioned, and C even contradicts the text.
« dormir peu passe encore pour une preuve d’énergie, voire de réussite. Tant que cette idée persistera, il est peu probable que les comportements changent ». Neither A nor B is mentioned.

« Je souhaite simplement qu’on les présente autrement… », ending with « Il est temps que l’on cesse de confondre… ». A is explicitly rejected: « Je ne demande pas qu’on cache les résultats »; C goes against the whole text’s position.
« ils mesurent surtout le profil des élèves qui entrent dans un lycée, et non ce que le lycée leur apporte ». Neither B nor C is mentioned.

« Je ne doute pas que cette demande soit légitime. Mais je doute fort qu’un rang dans un tableau les informe vraiment »: a partial concession followed by a rebuttal (note douter que + subjunctive). A: he doesn’t fully accept it; B: he explicitly quotes the other side’s argument.
« si bien que les écarts se creusent d’année en année » (si bien que introduces a result). Neither A nor C is mentioned.
« Il est temps que l’on cesse de… » is a clear call to action, and it describes the benefits of reform: the tone argues for change. There is no resignation (A) and no irony (B).
« Je voulais partager une belle découverte », ending with a suggestion that readers donate their unused tools: she is recommending the tool library. Neither B nor C is why she is writing.
« J’avais peur qu’on me prenne pour une incapable, car je n’avais jamais tenu une perceuse » (avoir peur que + subjunctive). A: the annual fee is only twenty francs; C isn’t mentioned.

« certains outils très demandés, comme la ponceuse, sont réservés des semaines à l’avance ». A contradicts the help from a “former carpenter”; B contradicts « chacun rapporte l’outil propre et vérifié ».
« Si vous en avez une qui dort dans un placard, pensez à la donner : elle sera bien plus utile là-bas »; là-bas refers to the tool library. Neither A nor C is mentioned.
« le bénévolat ne disparaît pas, il change de visage »: the whole interview is about how people take part differently. A isn’t mentioned; C: grant applications are only mentioned in passing.
« Le nombre de bénévoles reste à peu près stable ». B is the popular belief mentioned at the start, which he corrects; C has no basis.
« des emplois du temps plus morcelés, ils déménagent plus souvent, si bien qu’il leur est difficile de promettre une présence régulière ». Neither A nor B has any basis.
« certaines petites associations ont dû fermer, faute de président. Je crains que ce phénomène ne s’accentue ». B: he sees it as an opportunity; C isn’t mentioned.
« c’est aussi une porte d’entrée : un jeune qui vient aider une fois peut revenir, et peut-être prendre des responsabilités plus tard ». A is the opposite of his view; C isn’t mentioned.
« un service commun qui s’occupe de la comptabilité de vingt associations, de sorte que leurs bénévoles peuvent se consacrer à l’essentiel ». Neither A nor B is what the service does.
« absorbent la chaleur pendant la journée et la restituent la nuit, si bien que la ville ne se refroidit presque plus ». B gets the direction backwards; C has nothing to do with the concept.
« ce sont souvent les quartiers les plus denses et les plus pauvres qui souffrent le plus ». A is the opposite; C isn’t mentioned.
« remplacer le bitume des cours d’école par de la terre et de la végétation ». Neither A nor B is mentioned.
« parce qu’un arbre met vingt ans à donner de l’ombre ». Neither B nor C has any basis.
« a voté hier soir la création d’une prime à la réparation des vélos », covering half the repair cost. A isn’t mentioned; C is what the opposition wanted the money for, not what was decided.
« près d’un vélo sur trois reste au garage faute d’entretien, si bien que de nombreux habitants reprennent leur voiture ». B: there are twelve partner repair shops; C isn’t mentioned.
« elle aurait préféré que cet argent serve à sécuriser les pistes cyclables » (aurait préféré que + subjunctive). Neither A nor B is mentioned.

V39-01.zh: the adjustment variable, the first thing to be sacrificed
V39-01.exZh: When time runs short, sleep is often the first thing to be sacrificed.

V39-02.zh: to be singled out as the culprit
V39-02.exZh: Screens are singled out as the culprit for lack of sleep.

V39-03.exZh: Napping still has an image problem in the workplace.

V39-04.exZh: A simple awareness campaign isn’t enough to change habits fundamentally.

V39-05.exZh: Irregular working hours disrupt the sleep of many healthcare workers.

V39-06.exZh: The habit is so ingrained that people hardly dare criticise it.

V39-07.exZh: It’s time schools took children’s tiredness into account.

V39-08.zh: to take someone for an incompetent
V39-08.exZh: I was afraid these DIY experts would take me for someone who can’t do anything.

V39-09.zh: (an object) to sit unused in a cupboard
V39-09.exZh: My old sewing machine has been sitting unused in a cupboard for years.

V39-10.zh: to be designed in such a way that …
V39-10.exZh: These phones are designed in such a way that the battery can’t be replaced.

V39-11.zh: to change its face, to take on a new form
V39-11.exZh: With short-term assignments, volunteering is changing its face.

V39-12.exZh: The association is looking for volunteers willing to commit for the long term.

V39-13.exZh: With a fragmented schedule, it’s hard to promise to be there every week.

V39-14.zh: (something) to appeal to someone, to resonate
V39-14.exZh: A concrete project like renovating a school appeals to them more than meetings.

V39-15.exZh: Every association needs someone willing to keep the accounts.

V39-16.exZh: To attract people to lead associations, the administrative burden must be lightened.

V39-17.zh: to focus on what matters most
V39-17.exZh: Freed from bookkeeping, the volunteers can focus on what matters most.

V39-18.zh: to fear that … (+ subjunctive, can take expletive ne)
V39-18.exZh: I fear this phenomenon will grow in the coming years.

V39-19.exZh: A young tree takes years to give shade.

V39-20.zh: to find something hard to bear
V39-20.exZh: Elderly people find heatwave nights hard to bear.

V39-21.zh: to get someone back in the saddle (literally and figuratively)
V39-21.exZh: The grant aims to get occasional cyclists back in the saddle.

V39-22.zh: street furniture (benches, bus shelters, streetlights, etc.)
V39-22.exZh: Advertising pays for the upkeep of street furniture.

V39-23.zh: to come out on top, to be the winner
V39-23.exZh: Only the big chains will come out on top.

V39-24.exZh: Every bus shelter is also an advertising medium.

V39-25.zh: all it takes is … for … (both clauses + subjunctive)
V39-25.exZh: All it takes is one colleague with an allergy for everything to get complicated.
